name: Treatises on women's health
description: Foundational medieval medical writings on gynecology, obstetrics, menstruation, childbirth, and women's health, traditionally associated with Trota of Salerno.

name: Early childbirth pain relief methods
description: Described the use of plant-derived substances to relieve pain during childbirth and practical treatments for childbirth.

name: Menstrual health treatments
description: Described treatments intended to regulate menstruation, including the use of medicated pads or tampons.

name: Dermatological observations
description: Described dermatological manifestations of disease and contributed to early medical knowledge of skin conditions.

name: Sex chromosome determination
description: Demonstrated that chromosomes play a role in determining sex by identifying distinct chromosome types in male and female mealworms, providing foundational evidence for the XY sex-determination system.

name: Nuclear fission explanation
description: Provided the theoretical explanation for nuclear fission after Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann experimentally detected barium from irradiated uranium, recognizing that the uranium nucleus had split and released enormous energy.

name: Discovery of protactinium
description: Co-discovered protactinium, the chemical element with atomic number 91.

name: Auger effect
description: Independently discovered and explained the process in which atoms emit electrons after releasing excess energy.

name: Nuclear photographic emulsions
description: Developed highly sensitive photographic nuclear-emulsion techniques for detecting charged particles.

name: Disintegration stars
description: With Hertha Wambacher, observed characteristic disintegration stars produced when cosmic rays interacted with atomic nuclei.

name: Photomultiplier and scintillation counter methods
description: Was among the first physicists to propose combining early photomultiplier tubes with scintillation counters for particle detection.

name: DNA X-ray diffraction
description: Produced exceptionally important X-ray diffraction data on DNA, including Photograph 51, providing structural measurements crucial to determining DNA's molecular geometry.

name: DNA helical structure evidence
description: Used diffraction analysis to establish structural parameters demonstrating that DNA has a helical structure.

name: RNA virus structure
description: Made major contributions to understanding the structures of RNA viruses, particularly tobacco mosaic virus.

name: Pulsars
description: Discovered the first known pulsar in 1967 while analyzing radio-telescope recordings and recognizing an unusually regular repeating radio signal from the constellation Vulpecula.

name: Early pulsar observations
description: Helped identify additional pulsars and establish that the original repeating signal was astronomical rather than terrestrial interference.

name: Paired-associate learning paradigm
description: Developed an experimental method for studying memory in which participants learn associations between paired stimuli, becoming a classic paradigm in memory research.

name: Self-psychology
description: Developed a philosophical and psychological system treating the conscious self as central to psychological experience.

name: Cytogenetic basis of trisomy 21
description: Developed cell-culture and chromosome-analysis methods and observed that cells from patients with Down syndrome contained 47 chromosomes rather than 46, establishing the cytogenetic basis of trisomy 21.

name: Chromosome analysis in diagnosis
description: Helped establish chromosome counting and karyotyping as diagnostic methods for identifying chromosomal abnormalities.

name: Environmental enrichment and neuroplasticity
description: Demonstrated with collaborators that environmental conditions and experience can produce measurable structural changes in the mammalian cerebral cortex.

name: Lifespan neuroplasticity
description: Provided evidence that older brains can also undergo structural changes in response to environmental input.

name: Analysis of Einstein's brain
description: Analyzed preserved sections of Albert Einstein's brain and reported regional differences in glial-cell density, contributing to increased scientific attention to glia.

name: Lambda phage
description: Discovered bacteriophage lambda, a virus that infects E. coli, and investigated its lysogenic behavior.

name: F fertility factor
description: Identified the bacterial F factor, later understood as genetic material enabling bacterial conjugation.

name: Replica plating
description: Developed and implemented replica plating with Joshua Lederberg, allowing bacterial colonies to be transferred while preserving their spatial arrangement.

name: Specialized transduction
description: Contributed to understanding how bacteriophages can transfer particular bacterial genes between cells.

name: Transposable genetic elements
description: Demonstrated that genetic elements can move to different positions on chromosomes and alter the expression of nearby genes.

name: Activator and Dissociation elements
description: Identified the Activator (Ac) and Dissociation (Ds) elements in maize and demonstrated that their movement could alter genes controlling kernel pigmentation.

name: Chromosome breakage studies
description: Characterized the behavior of the Dissociation element and showed that it could cause chromosome breakage at particular sites.

name: Cytogenetic mapping
description: Developed detailed methods for correlating visible chromosome structures with genetic traits and tracking chromosome behavior during inheritance.

name: Genome regulation
description: Demonstrated that genomes are dynamically regulated rather than consisting of genes fixed permanently in immutable positions.

name: Noether's theorem
description: Established the fundamental relationship between continuous symmetries and conservation laws, including the relationship between time symmetry and energy conservation.

name: Noetherian rings
description: Formalized the ascending-chain condition on ideals, creating a foundational concept in commutative algebra.

name: Ideal theory
description: Developed structural approaches to the study of ideals in rings, helping shift algebra toward the study of general mathematical structures.

name: Invariant theory
description: Made major contributions to the study of mathematical quantities and structures that remain invariant under transformations.

name: Cori cycle
description: Demonstrated the metabolic relationship between muscle and liver in carbohydrate metabolism, in which lactate produced by muscle is transported to the liver and converted toward glucose.

name: Glucose-1-phosphate / Cori ester
description: With Carl Cori, identified glucose-1-phosphate as a key intermediate in glycogen breakdown.

name: Glycogen phosphorylase
description: Helped identify and characterize glycogen phosphorylase, the enzyme responsible for initiating glycogen breakdown.

name: Enzyme regulation
description: Contributed to the discovery that glycogen phosphorylase exists in different functional forms and helped establish principles of enzyme activation and inactivation.

name: In-vitro glycogen synthesis
description: Demonstrated experimentally that glycogen could be synthesized, helping establish biochemical pathways as sequences of enzyme-catalyzed reactions.
